=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s “standard/cleared” labels should not be accepted as determinative. Several provisions materially shift pre-Completion risk to Wattlebridge and undermine the debt-free/cash-free deal.

### 1. Liability caps and survival

**Seller position:** General warranty cap of AUD 4.8m, AUD 25,000 de minimis, AUD 250,000 basket, 18-month survival, with the same regime applying to title and capacity.

**Push back:**

- Title, capacity, authority and no-encumbrance claims should be **fundamental warranties**, with a cap of at least the purchase price—and preferably uncapped for fraud, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment.
- Fundamental warranties should survive for the applicable statutory limitation period, or at least 6–7 years.
- Tax warranties/indemnities should have a separate, longer survival period.
- The general cap should be negotiated upward, particularly given the known Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and privacy exposures.
- De minimis should apply per claim, but not prevent aggregation of related claims.
- The basket should be a **tipping basket**, or at minimum the Seller should bear the full amount once the threshold is exceeded. The proposed “excess only” basket is buyer-unfriendly.
- Fraud, wilful breach, deliberate non-disclosure, fundamental warranties, tax, title, leakage, debt-like items and specific indemnities should be outside the general limitations.

### 2. General disclosure and buyer knowledge

The proposed disclosure is substantially too broad.

The Seller purports to disclose the entire data room, public registers and all matters discoverable by the Buyer or its advisers. That would:

- convert an unfiltered data room into a blanket disclosure;
- make it difficult to establish breach even where the relevant information is buried in a document;
- deprive the Buyer of warranty protection for matters it did not actually appreciate; and
- potentially treat incomplete or ambiguous documents as effective disclosure.

**Push back:**

- Disclosure must be **fair, specific and reasonably comprehensible**, identifying the relevant warranty and the actual implications.
- General disclosure should be limited to clearly identified documents in an agreed index, not every fact “contained or referred to” in the data room.
- Buyer knowledge should mean actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer representatives, without constructive knowledge or knowledge attributed merely from advisers or data-room availability.
- No waiver should arise where the disclosure is incomplete, qualified, contradictory or fails to identify the relevant risk.
- The Seller should warrant that the data room is complete and accurate in all material respects and that no material information has been withheld.
- Require a bring-down confirmation at Completion, with any new disclosure giving the Buyer a termination or price-adjustment right.

### 3. Bluefen — major Completion risk

Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. Consent has not been obtained and conditions remain unsatisfied.

Delivery of a purported consent should not automatically satisfy the condition if the consent is conditional or ineffective.

**Require:**

- final written consent before Completion;
- evidence that every condition in clause 11.3 has been satisfied or waived in writing;
- a condition precedent in favour of the Buyer, capable of waiver only by the Buyer;
- a long-stop date and termination right;
- a specific indemnity for loss arising from failure to obtain consent, termination, reduced revenue or customer claims; and
- a warranty that Bluefen has not threatened termination or renegotiation.

Given the revenue concentration, the Buyer should consider a price reduction, retention or escrow if consent is not unconditional.

### 4. Riverlark — inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free

The AUD 3.2m facility remains outstanding and security has not been discharged. A post-Completion release is unacceptable.

This creates a direct risk that the Buyer acquires the Company while debt and security remain in place.

**Require before Completion:**

- full repayment of the facility;
- payoff letter from Riverlark;
- release of all guarantees, security interests and other encumbrances;
- ASIC/PPSR and other relevant discharge evidence;
- confirmation that no break costs, fees or contingent liabilities remain; and
- a Seller-funded indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability.

The amount should be reflected in the funds flow or treated as a purchase-price adjustment/debt-like item. Consider a retention until all releases are verified.

### 5. Completion bonuses — undisclosed transaction liability

The AUD 420,000 bonuses are conditional on Completion and are absent from the funds flow. They appear to be a transaction-related liability triggered by the sale, not an ordinary operating expense.

**Require:**

- inclusion in the Completion funds flow;
- Seller payment before or at Completion;
- Seller responsibility for payroll tax, superannuation, withholding and all associated on-costs;
- confirmation that no additional bonuses, retention payments or change-of-control payments exist; and
- an indemnity for any employee claim or statutory liability.

The amount should not reduce the Buyer’s working-capital position or be left for the Company to fund after Completion.

### 6. Ironquay IP and SOW3

The Seller’s proposed indemnity limited to the AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment is inadequate. Payment may be necessary but may not by itself resolve ownership, assignment or infringement risk.

**Require:**

- payment or escrow of the disputed amount;
- executed assignment and delivery of all SOW3 materials;
- confirmation of chain of title, waivers and third-party consents;
- warranties that the Company owns or has valid rights to all relevant IP;
- coverage for infringement, re-performance, customer claims, remediation and all associated costs; and
- a specific indemnity outside the general cap and basket until the matter is fully resolved.

### 7. Export/privacy incident

This is potentially a material privacy and cybersecurity issue, not merely an “operational matter.” The data may include personal information, and the facts do not establish whether unauthorised access occurred or whether notification obligations have been met.

**Require before Completion:**

- full incident report and forensic findings;
- confirmation of containment, access logs and affected individuals;
- assessment under the Privacy Act and Notifiable Data Breaches regime;
- confirmation of any regulator, customer or individual notifications;
- remediation and monitoring plan;
- cyber-insurance details; and
- a specific indemnity for notification, investigation, remediation, regulatory, litigation and customer costs.

The Buyer should reserve a right to delay or terminate Completion if the incident is material or unresolved. This exposure should not be subject to the general cap, basket or 18-month period.

### 8. Supplier renewals — AUD 330,000

The disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are binding, unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Calling them “ordinary-course operating costs” does not resolve the economic impact.

**Require:**

- copies of the executed renewals;
- confirmation of commencement dates, termination rights and minimum commitments;
- identification of any prepayments, break fees or change-of-control provisions;
- treatment of accrued amounts in working capital/debt-like calculations; and
- Seller payment or price adjustment for commitments entered into outside the ordinary course or without Buyer approval.

The Buyer should receive a warranty that no material supplier commitment has been entered into since the agreed accounts date without consent.

### 9. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures do not establish whether a notification obligation has been complied with, whether consent is required, or whether a change of control triggers assignment restrictions.

**Require:**

- review of the complete lease and Mossvale agreement;
- written landlord/counterparty consent or waiver where required;
- confirmation that no default, termination right or rent review has been triggered;
- warranties covering change-of-control provisions; and
- indemnities for any pre-Completion breach or resulting termination.

These should be Completion deliverables where consent is required, not matters left for post-Completion regularisation.

### 10. Title to shares

A share register alone is not enough. It does not necessarily establish that the shares are fully paid, beneficially owned, free from encumbrances or transferable without restriction.

**Require warranties and evidence that:**

- Seller is the legal and beneficial owner of all shares;
- shares are fully paid and comprise the entire issued capital;
- no options, convertibles, trusts, pre-emption rights or third-party interests exist;
- shares are free of all security interests and other encumbrances;
- all corporate approvals and transfer documents are valid; and
- the Buyer receives updated registers, certificates and ASIC records at Completion.

### 11. Tax and IP

The statement that tax and IP are “settled under the general regime” should be rejected. These are core diligence areas and should not be confined to a low general cap and short survival period.

**Require:**

- a standalone tax covenant/indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, payroll tax, GST, penalties and interest;
- specific IP ownership, infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignment warranties;
- separate caps and survival periods; and
- no exclusion merely because an issue was generally disclosed unless it was fairly and specifically disclosed.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Condition Completion** on Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/release and required landlord/customer consents.  
2. **Correct the funds flow** for the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all transaction-related costs.  
3. Obtain specific indemnities for Riverlark, Ironquay, the privacy incident and employee bonuses.  
4. Reject blanket data-room disclosure, broad constructive knowledge and all-claims non-reliance.  
5. Preserve separate, higher/uncapped protection for title, authority, tax, IP, fraud and deliberate concealment.  
6. Increase the general cap, improve the basket, and extend survival periods.  
7. Obtain complete supporting documents and written confirmations before signing or Completion.  
8. Use a retention/escrow or price adjustment for unresolved exposures, particularly Bluefen, Riverlark and the privacy incident.
